concepts.title: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
concepts.definition: Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity, with high melting points and sonority; non-metals are mostly brittle, dull and poor conductors - though exceptions like graphite conducting electricity and iodine's lustre remind us the rules bend.
concepts.key_idea: Shine, bend, conduct - metals; brittle and dull - non-metals; but every rule has exceptions.
question_patterns: list the physical properties of metals and non-metals
why are metals used to make electric wires - explain ductility and conductivity
name the most ductile and the best conductor metal
classify the given elements as metals or non-metals from their properties

solution_steps.explain: Check lustre, malleability, ductility and conduction.
Note brittleness, dullness and poor conduction.
Graphite conducts; iodine shines - exceptions complete the picture.

concepts.title: Chemical Properties - Reactions of Metals
concepts.definition: Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides, with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen, and with dilute acids to release hydrogen; their vigour follows the reactivity series, where potassium races and gold refuses.
concepts.key_idea: The reactivity series ranks the race: potassium to gold, each metal knows its place.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc103.txt sections on chemical properties and reactivity series
question_patterns: write the reactions of metals with oxygen, water and dilute acids

solution_steps.explain: List metals from most to least reactive.
Only metals above hydrogen release hydrogen from acids.
Oxides, hydroxides and salts form with hydrogen evolution.

concepts.title: Metallurgy - Extraction and Corrosion
concepts.definition: Metallurgy extracts metals from their ores in steps matched to reactivity: roasting or calcination converts ores to oxides, reduction frees the metal, and refining polishes it by electrolysis; finally, alloying and galvanising guard metals from corrosion like rust.
concepts.key_idea: Extract by reactivity, refine by electrolysis, protect by alloying and coating.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc103.txt sections on metallurgy, corrosion and its prevention
question_patterns: describe the steps of extracting a metal from its ore

solution_steps.explain: Remove gangue based on the ore's nature.
Roast or calcine to oxide, then reduce by carbon, heat or electrolysis.
Electrolytic refining purifies; alloys and coatings prevent corrosion.
